name: Healthcare
title: Referral coordination evidence desk
summary: Prepare complete referral packets and scheduling options while clinicians retain clinical decisions and care priorities.
situation: Illustrative architecture: A hospital network receives specialty referrals with scanned attachments, incomplete records, and differing scheduling requirements. Coordinators need to locate missing administrative evidence without exposing unrelated patient records. This illustrative architecture supports referral operations; it does not diagnose, triage emergencies, or recommend treatment.
problem: Patient identity mismatches and incomplete referral documentation create repeated handoffs. A model may incorrectly interpret missing information as a negative finding or mistake a scheduling preference for a clinical instruction. Administrative automation must preserve these distinctions.
whyAgents: Specialists separately verify record identity, retrieve permitted documents, check locally defined packet requirements, and prepare scheduling choices. Clinical urgency and suitability remain explicit inputs from authorized clinicians, never inferred scheduling shortcuts.
outcome: The intended result is a reviewable operational decision with source evidence and explicit ownership. Measure coordinator effort and documentation completeness alongside privacy and wrong-patient incidents. Scheduling speed alone is insufficient: the workflow must preserve clinician ownership and keep every unresolved item visible until a responsible person closes it.

agents.name: Identity reconciliation agent
agents.responsibility: Compare referral identifiers with the patient index and surface possible mismatches.
agents.boundary: Cannot merge patient records or select among ambiguous identities.

agents.name: Record retrieval agent
agents.responsibility: Collect the minimum authorized documents for the referral purpose with provenance.
agents.boundary: Cannot retrieve unrelated encounters or alter clinical notes.

agents.name: Completeness reviewer
agents.responsibility: Compare supplied documents with clinician-approved administrative requirements.
agents.boundary: Flags missing evidence without interpreting clinical adequacy.

agents.name: Scheduling assistant
agents.responsibility: Prepare available appointment options consistent with recorded clinician instructions.
agents.boundary: Cannot change urgency, issue clinical advice, or book outside approved coordinator actions.

systems.name: Electronic health record
systems.role: Authoritative patient identifiers and clinical records behind purpose-aware access controls.

systems.name: Referral management platform
systems.role: Owns referral state, responsible coordinator, clinician instructions, and outstanding document requests.

systems.name: Scheduling and consent services
systems.role: Supply appointment availability and permission context; bookings use an approved transactional adapter.

flow.title: Register referral
flow.description: Validate referring organization, patient identifiers, requested specialty, and assigned coordinator before creating a durable referral case.

flow.title: Resolve identity
flow.description: Check the patient index deterministically; route ambiguous matches to trained staff without gathering candidate charts into a model prompt.

flow.title: Retrieve permitted evidence
flow.description: Fetch only documents relevant to the referral purpose and capture record versions, provenance, and access decisions.

flow.title: Check packet requirements
flow.description: Apply the approved administrative checklist; distinguish missing, unavailable, and explicitly documented information in the draft.

flow.title: Prepare coordinator choices
flow.description: Present outstanding requests and appointment options while displaying clinician-supplied urgency and any unresolved identity issue.

flow.title: Commit approved scheduling
flow.description: Recheck consent and slot availability, execute an approved booking once, then record the receipt and pending follow-up responsibilities.

failures.detection: Identifier checks fail to establish a unique permitted chart match.
failures.recovery: Suspend retrieval and route identity resolution to the hospital's existing registration process.

failures.scenario: An appointment slot disappears during review.
failures.detection: Booking adapter rejects the previously displayed availability version.
failures.recovery: Refresh options and return to the coordinator without silently substituting a different appointment.

controls: Apply patient, organization, and purpose-of-use authorization before every document retrieval.
Keep clinical urgency and treatment decisions under qualified clinician control.
Show missing data as missing; never generate normal findings from absence.
Exclude clinical document text from general application logs and tracing attributes.
Bind scheduling approval to patient, specialty, slot, and current permission context.

metrics.name: Packet completeness
metrics.definition: Referrals meeting the approved administrative checklist divided by referrals submitted for coordinator review.

metrics.name: Identity escalation rate
metrics.definition: Referrals requiring manual identity resolution divided by received referrals, monitored by source organization.

metrics.name: Coordination lead time
metrics.definition: Elapsed time from referral receipt to a coordinator-approved next step, with patient waiting time reported separately.

metrics.name: Booking reconciliation rate
metrics.definition: Booking attempts with uncertain or conflicting receipts divided by approved booking attempts.

tradeoffs.cost: Additional authorized retrieval may be needed when requirements change.
Clinical interpretation still requires separate clinician workflow.
Displayed options may expire and require another interaction.

rollout.acceptance: Staff verify identity ambiguity, missing-document labeling, and forbidden clinical advice cases without patient data.
Approved users inspect live packets after access, provenance, and audit checks pass.
One specialty enables coordinator-approved booking after consent changes and slot-race recovery are demonstrated.
